\section{Task}\label{task}

\textbf{Validation of the models against observational data. Random and
Systematic Discrepancies.}

Note: When answering the above-mentioned research questions, the focus
should be on the methodological aspects of the respective model
applications and the necessary analyses. A detailed answer to the
questions in the context of other scientific work goes beyond the scope
of this course.

Portfolio: Description of methods, results and a (short) discussion. The
important thing is the complete documentation of the conducted model
simulations.

\subsection{Data Preparation}\label{data-preparation}

The required format of data for the LakeEnsemblR model environment are
\emph{.csv} tables containing the pond hypsograph, the water temperature
profile of the pond and the meteorological data. These files are
prepared using the following code from the given datasets.

\subsection{Observed Data Preparation}\label{observed-data-preparation}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# turn wide format of EERES Temperature to long format}
\NormalTok{EERES\_Temperature }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read\_csv}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Data/EERES\_Temperature.csv"}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## Rows: 43067 Columns: 8
## -- Column specification --------------------------------------------------------
## Delimiter: ","
## chr (1): time
## dbl (7): 30 cm, 25 cm, 20 cm, 15 cm, 10 cm, 5 cm, air
## 
## i Use `spec()` to retrieve the full column specification for this data.
## i Specify the column types or set `show_col_types = FALSE` to quiet this message.
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{EERES\_T\_long }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{pivot\_longer}\NormalTok{(EERES\_Temperature, }\AttributeTok{cols=}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\AttributeTok{30 cm}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\SpecialCharTok{:}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\AttributeTok{air}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{names\_to =} \StringTok{"Depth\_meter"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{values\_to =} \StringTok{"Water\_Temperature\_celsius"}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{!}\NormalTok{Depth\_meter}\SpecialCharTok{==}\StringTok{"air"}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{datetime =} \FunctionTok{dmy\_hm}\NormalTok{(time),}
         \AttributeTok{Depth\_meter =}  \FunctionTok{gsub}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"[\^{}0{-}9]"}\NormalTok{, }\StringTok{""}\NormalTok{, Depth\_meter)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{Depth\_meter =} \FunctionTok{as.numeric}\NormalTok{(Depth\_meter)}\SpecialCharTok{/}\DecValTok{100}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{time) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(datetime, Depth\_meter, Water\_Temperature\_celsius) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{!}\FunctionTok{is.na}\NormalTok{(Water\_Temperature\_celsius)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{datetime =} \FunctionTok{format}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{floor\_date}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{as\_datetime}\NormalTok{(datetime), }\AttributeTok{unit=}\StringTok{"10 minutes"}\NormalTok{),}\StringTok{"\%Y{-}\%m{-}\%d \%H:\%M:\%S"}\NormalTok{))}

\CommentTok{\# Optionally discard the Temperature at 15cm depth due to missing data}

\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Interpolation of missing
data}\label{interpolation-of-missing-data}

To fill the observations the missing data at the depth of 15cm is
interpolated from the temperature observations 5cm above and below. This
can be subsequentially used if required by the models.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# interpolation of missing data at 15cm depth \#\#\#\#}
\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# from adjacent depths                        \#\#\#\#}

\CommentTok{\# Function to interpolate temperature for NA values at Depth\_meter = 0.15}
\NormalTok{interpolate\_na\_temperature }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \ControlFlowTok{function}\NormalTok{(data) \{}
  \CommentTok{\# Filter for the specific datetime and depth}
\NormalTok{  temp\_data }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ data }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(Depth\_meter }\SpecialCharTok{\%in\%} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\FloatTok{0.1}\NormalTok{, }\FloatTok{0.2}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\&} \SpecialCharTok{!}\FunctionTok{is.na}\NormalTok{(Water\_Temperature\_celsius))}
  
  \ControlFlowTok{if}\NormalTok{ (}\FunctionTok{nrow}\NormalTok{(temp\_data) }\SpecialCharTok{==} \DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{) \{}
    \CommentTok{\# Perform linear interpolation}
\NormalTok{    interpolated\_temp }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{approx}\NormalTok{(temp\_data}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{Depth\_meter, temp\_data}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{Water\_Temperature\_celsius, }\AttributeTok{xout =} \FloatTok{0.15}\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{y}
    \FunctionTok{return}\NormalTok{(interpolated\_temp)}
\NormalTok{  \} }\ControlFlowTok{else}\NormalTok{ \{}
    \FunctionTok{return}\NormalTok{(}\ConstantTok{NA}\NormalTok{)  }\CommentTok{\# Return NA if not enough data for interpolation}
\NormalTok{  \}}
\NormalTok{\}}

\CommentTok{\# Apply interpolation only for NA values at Depth\_meter = 0.15}
\NormalTok{EERES\_T\_long }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ EERES\_T\_long }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{group\_by}\NormalTok{(datetime) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{Water\_Temperature\_celsius =} \FunctionTok{ifelse}\NormalTok{(Depth\_meter }\SpecialCharTok{==} \FloatTok{0.15} \SpecialCharTok{\&} \FunctionTok{is.na}\NormalTok{(Water\_Temperature\_celsius),}
                                             \FunctionTok{interpolate\_na\_temperature}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{cur\_data}\NormalTok{()),}
\NormalTok{                                             Water\_Temperature\_celsius)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{ungroup}\NormalTok{()}


\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# write water temperature to .csv file \#\#\#\#}

\CommentTok{\# write.table(EERES\_T\_long, file = "LakeEnsemblR\_wtemp\_profile\_EERES.csv", sep = ",", dec = ".", row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE)}

\CommentTok{\# write.table(EERES\_T\_dropNAcol, file = "LakeEnsemblR\_wtemp\_profile\_EERES.csv", sep = ",", dec = ".", row.names = FALSE, col.names = TRUE, quote = FALSE)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\subsection{Meteo Data Preparation}\label{meteo-data-preparation}

Following code presents the preparation of the meteorological data. This
was done by aggregating the meteorological data to the temporal scale of
the observed data (1min to 10min). Therefore averaging the parameters
and summing of the parameter rainfall in mm per hour was applied.
LakeEnsemblR requires an input of surface level barometric pressure in
Pa, therefore the transformation from hPa tp Pa was undertaken. The wind
direction and speed at 10m above surface is required for the
meteorolgical forcing data. The exact location of the anemometer was not
known, hence it was assumed that the given data reflects this
requirement.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# Loading meteorological data \#\#\#\#}

\NormalTok{meteo\_raw }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read\_xlsx}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"Data/20200101{-}20211231\_Wetterstationsdaten\_Andreas Lorke.xlsx"}\NormalTok{, }
    \AttributeTok{skip =} \DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{na=}\FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"{-}99999.9"}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{"{-}9999"}\NormalTok{)) }
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## New names:
## * `~` -> `~...1`
## * `~` -> `~...2`
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{meteo }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ meteo\_raw }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{as.data.frame}\NormalTok{() }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{across}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{where}\NormalTok{(is.numeric), }\SpecialCharTok{\textasciitilde{}} \FunctionTok{na\_if}\NormalTok{(., }\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\DecValTok{9999}\NormalTok{))) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}      \CommentTok{\# NAs}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{across}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{where}\NormalTok{(is.numeric), }\SpecialCharTok{\textasciitilde{}} \FunctionTok{na\_if}\NormalTok{(., }\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\FloatTok{99999.9}\NormalTok{))) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}   \CommentTok{\# NAs}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{time=}\FunctionTok{format}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{as\_datetime}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\AttributeTok{\textasciitilde{}...1}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{),}\StringTok{"\%H:\%M:\%S"}\NormalTok{),}
         \AttributeTok{date=}\FunctionTok{format}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{as\_datetime}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\AttributeTok{\textasciitilde{}...2}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{),}\StringTok{"\%Y{-}\%m{-}\%d"}\NormalTok{)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}                      
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{datetime=}\FunctionTok{ymd}\NormalTok{(date) }\SpecialCharTok{+} \FunctionTok{hms}\NormalTok{(time))}

\CommentTok{\# check for na values in all columns but the wind direction column WV}
\NormalTok{na\_df }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ meteo }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(SO,TE,FE,TP,WD,WR,RD,DR,RE) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{if\_any}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{everything}\NormalTok{(), is.na))}


\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# Aggregating the meteorological data to 10 minute intervals \#\#\#\#}

\NormalTok{meteo\_10m\_t }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ meteo }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \CommentTok{\# Melt the data to long format}
  \FunctionTok{pivot\_longer}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{cols =} \SpecialCharTok{{-}}\FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(datetime,}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\AttributeTok{\textasciitilde{}...1}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\AttributeTok{\textasciitilde{}...2}\StringTok{\textasciigrave{}}\NormalTok{,time,date), }\AttributeTok{names\_to =} \StringTok{"variable"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{values\_to =} \StringTok{"value"}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \CommentTok{\# Create time groups by flooring the datetime to 10minute sets}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{time\_group =} \FunctionTok{floor\_date}\NormalTok{(datetime, }\AttributeTok{unit =} \StringTok{"10 minutes"}\NormalTok{)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \CommentTok{\# Group by time\_group and variable}
  \FunctionTok{group\_by}\NormalTok{(time\_group, variable) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \CommentTok{\# Summarise the data to ensure a single value per group}
  \FunctionTok{summarise}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{value =} \FunctionTok{ifelse}\NormalTok{(variable }\SpecialCharTok{==} \StringTok{"RD"}\NormalTok{, }\FunctionTok{sum}\NormalTok{(value, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{), }\FunctionTok{mean}\NormalTok{(value, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{)), }
            \AttributeTok{.groups =} \StringTok{"drop"}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \CommentTok{\# Gather back to wide format, ensuring unique values}
  \FunctionTok{pivot\_wider}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{names\_from =}\NormalTok{ variable, }\AttributeTok{values\_from =}\NormalTok{ value, }\AttributeTok{values\_fn =} \FunctionTok{list}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{value =}\NormalTok{ mean))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## Warning: Returning more (or less) than 1 row per `summarise()` group was deprecated in
## dplyr 1.1.0.
## i Please use `reframe()` instead.
## i When switching from `summarise()` to `reframe()`, remember that `reframe()`
##   always returns an ungrouped data frame and adjust accordingly.
## Call `lifecycle::last_lifecycle_warnings()` to see where this warning was
## generated.
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# Adding missing time steps for proper model functioning \#\#\#\#}

\CommentTok{\# fill missing steps in time series of meteo data}
\NormalTok{complete\_time\_series }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{seq}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{from =} \FunctionTok{min}\NormalTok{(meteo\_10m\_t}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{time\_group, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{), }
                  \AttributeTok{to =} \FunctionTok{max}\NormalTok{(meteo\_10m\_t}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{time\_group, }\AttributeTok{na.rm =} \ConstantTok{TRUE}\NormalTok{), }
                  \AttributeTok{by =} \StringTok{"10 min"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{meteo\_complete }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{data.frame}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{time\_group=}\NormalTok{complete\_time\_series) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{full\_join}\NormalTok{(meteo\_10m\_t, }\AttributeTok{by =} \StringTok{"time\_group"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{meteo\_filled }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ meteo\_complete }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
\CommentTok{\#interpolate values}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{across}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(time\_group, WV), }\SpecialCharTok{\textasciitilde{}}\NormalTok{ zoo}\SpecialCharTok{::}\FunctionTok{na.approx}\NormalTok{(.))) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(time\_group,SO,TE,FE,TP,WD,WR,RD,DR) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
\CommentTok{\#hPa to Pa}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{DR =} \DecValTok{100}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{DR) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
\CommentTok{\#mm/10min to mm/hr}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{RD =} \DecValTok{6}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{RD) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
\CommentTok{\#rename and restructure to LakeEnsemblR Standard}
  \FunctionTok{rename}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{datetime=}\NormalTok{time\_group,}
  \AttributeTok{Shortwave\_Radiation\_Downwelling\_wattPerMeterSquared=}\NormalTok{SO,}
  \AttributeTok{Air\_Temperature\_celsius=}\NormalTok{TE,}
  \AttributeTok{Relative\_Humidity\_percent=}\NormalTok{FE,}
  \AttributeTok{Dewpoint\_Temperature\_celsius=}\NormalTok{TP,}
  \AttributeTok{Ten\_Meter\_Elevation\_Wind\_Speed\_meterPerSecond=}\NormalTok{WD,}
  \AttributeTok{Ten\_Meter\_Elevation\_Wind\_Direction\_degree=}\NormalTok{WR,}
  \AttributeTok{Rainfall\_millimeterPerHour=}\NormalTok{RD,}
  \AttributeTok{Surface\_Level\_Barometric\_Pressure\_pascal=}\NormalTok{DR) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{mutate}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{datetime =} \FunctionTok{format}\NormalTok{(datetime, }\StringTok{"\%Y{-}\%m{-}\%d \%H:\%M:\%S"}\NormalTok{)) }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(datetime,Ten\_Meter\_Elevation\_Wind\_Speed\_meterPerSecond,Air\_Temperature\_celsius,Relative\_Humidity\_percent,Shortwave\_Radiation\_Downwelling\_wattPerMeterSquared,Surface\_Level\_Barometric\_Pressure\_pascal,Rainfall\_millimeterPerHour)}

\CommentTok{\# check for remaining NAs}
\NormalTok{meteo\_filled }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%}
  \FunctionTok{filter}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{if\_any}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{everything}\NormalTok{(), is.na))}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\section{Model}\label{model}

\subsection{Ensemble model run}\label{ensemble-model-run}

Following Code runs the LER model using a default calibration of the
model parameters.

There are issues using GLM and MyLake in shallow ponds, therefore all
following simulations are done using exclusively FLake, GOTM or
Simstrat.

We found that the model FLake calculates a mean depth of the lake from
the volume (calculated from truncated square pyramids between the
layers) and the surface area. This however seems to reduce the depth of
shallow ponds below the depths of observed layers. Therefore we manually
set the depth of the pond for FLake using the parameter
\texttt{depth\_w\_lk}.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# ensure the working directory is properly set \#\#\#\#}

\FunctionTok{getwd}\NormalTok{()}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
## [1] "C:/Users/morit/Documents/ACP5_PondModel"
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# setwd("../")}
\CommentTok{\# Set config file \& models}
\NormalTok{config\_file }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \StringTok{"LakeEnsemblR\_EERES.yaml"}
\CommentTok{\# model \textless{}{-} c("FLake", "GLM", "GOTM", "Simstrat",  "MyLake")}
\NormalTok{model }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"FLake"}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{"GOTM"}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{"Simstrat"}\NormalTok{)}



\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# Create configuration and run LER \#\#\#\#}

\CommentTok{\# Default run}
\CommentTok{\# 1. Export settings {-} creates directories with all model setups and exports settings from the LER configuration file}
\FunctionTok{export\_config}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{config\_file =}\NormalTok{ config\_file, }\AttributeTok{model =}\NormalTok{ model)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

## 1   0.30 20.49
## 2   0.25 20.56
## 3   0.20 20.63
## 4   0.15 20.68
## 5   0.10 20.69

\begin{Shaded}

\subsection{Calibration}\label{calibration}

The calibration is done using the function \texttt{cali\_ensemble}. Due
to errors by using this function on all models simultaneously, the
results will be generated for each model individually For each model, a
calibration using a set of 500 parameter combinations is used for the
models Simstrat and GOTM. For FLake only 100 parameter combinations were
used due to technical obstacles. A Latin Hypercube Calibration (LHC)
method is used in the calibration. With the function \texttt{plot\_LHC},
the results can be shown graphically.

Depending on some arguments given to \texttt{cali\_ensemble} (we guess
\texttt{parallel\ =\ True}), the output of the function will either be
the results or the names of the .csv files which store the parameter
sets and results. Due to this inconsistency in the code, we manually
select the generated results from the folder /\emph{cali}.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# Function to retrieve model fit \#\#\#\#}

\CommentTok{\# getting the model fit of the last ensemble run}
\FunctionTok{calc\_fit}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{ncdf =} \StringTok{"output/ensemble\_output.nc"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{model =}\NormalTok{ model)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

Since the inherent method of using a single model perfomance metric to
derive the set of parameters with the best performance is rather
arbitrary, we decided to develop a more systematic approach to identify
the model parameters with the best fit.

The simulations using different sets of parameters were subsequently
analyzed, aiming to identify parameter values which minimize deviations
from observed data. For this purpose a composite error metric combining
RMSE, NSE, Bias and R² was calculated. Parameter values which minimized
this composite score were chosen as the calibrated value.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{params\_Sim }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"cali/params\_Simstrat\_LHC\_n500.csv"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{em\_Sim }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"cali/Simstrat\_LHC\_n500.csv"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{params\_GOTM }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"cali/params\_GOTM\_LHC\_n500.csv"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{em\_GOTM }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"cali/GOTM\_LHC\_n500.csv"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{params\_FLake }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"cali/params\_FLake\_LHC\_n100.csv"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{em\_FLake }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{read.csv}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"cali/FLake\_LHC\_n100.csv"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{join\_Sim }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{full\_join}\NormalTok{(params\_Sim, em\_Sim, }\AttributeTok{by =} \StringTok{"par\_id"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{join\_GOTM }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{full\_join}\NormalTok{(params\_GOTM, em\_GOTM, }\AttributeTok{by =} \StringTok{"par\_id"}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{join\_FLake }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{full\_join}\NormalTok{(params\_FLake, em\_FLake, }\AttributeTok{by =} \StringTok{"par\_id"}\NormalTok{)}


\DocumentationTok{\#\# Merge data sets for calibration of shared parameters}
\NormalTok{Sim\_red }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ join\_Sim }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{a\_seiche, }\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{par\_id)}
\NormalTok{GOTM\_red }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ join\_GOTM }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{turb\_param.k\_min, }\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{par\_id)}
\NormalTok{FLake\_red }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ join\_FLake }\SpecialCharTok{\%\textgreater{}\%} \FunctionTok{select}\NormalTok{(}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{c\_relax\_C, }\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{par\_id)}

\NormalTok{shared }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{rbind}\NormalTok{(Sim\_red, GOTM\_red, FLake\_red)}



\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\# Calculate composite error metric score \#\#\#\#}

\DocumentationTok{\#\# Weights (scaled with standard deviation to approximate equal influence of individual metrics)}
\NormalTok{w1 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse) }\CommentTok{\# RMSE}
\NormalTok{w2 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{((}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse)) }\CommentTok{\# NSE}
\NormalTok{w3 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias)) }\CommentTok{\# Bias}
\NormalTok{w4 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r) }\CommentTok{\# R\^{}2}

\DocumentationTok{\#\# Compisite error metric}
\NormalTok{join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{score }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ w1}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w2}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w3}\SpecialCharTok{*}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w4}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ join\_Sim}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r)}


\DocumentationTok{\#\# Weights (scaled with standard deviation to approximate equal influence of individual metrics)}
\NormalTok{w5 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse) }\CommentTok{\# RMSE}
\NormalTok{w6 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{((}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse)) }\CommentTok{\# NSE}
\NormalTok{w7 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias)) }\CommentTok{\# Bias}
\NormalTok{w8 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r) }\CommentTok{\# R\^{}2}

\DocumentationTok{\#\# Compisite error metric}
\NormalTok{join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{score }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ w5}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w6}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w7}\SpecialCharTok{*}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w8}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ join\_GOTM}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r)}


\DocumentationTok{\#\# Weights (scaled with standard deviation to approximate equal influence of individual metrics)}
\NormalTok{w9 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse) }\CommentTok{\# RMSE}
\NormalTok{w10 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{((}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse)) }\CommentTok{\# NSE}
\NormalTok{w11 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias)) }\CommentTok{\# Bias}
\NormalTok{w12 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r) }\CommentTok{\# R\^{}2}

\DocumentationTok{\#\# Compisite error metric}
\NormalTok{join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{score }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ w9}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w10}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w11}\SpecialCharTok{*}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w12}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ join\_FLake}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r)}


\DocumentationTok{\#\# Weights (scaled with standard deviation to approximate equal influence of individual metrics)}
\NormalTok{w13 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse) }\CommentTok{\# RMSE}
\NormalTok{w14 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{((}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse)) }\CommentTok{\# NSE}
\NormalTok{w15 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias)) }\CommentTok{\# Bias}
\NormalTok{w16 }\OtherTok{=} \DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{/}\FunctionTok{sd}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r) }\CommentTok{\# R\^{}2}

\DocumentationTok{\#\# Compisite error metric}
\NormalTok{shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{score }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ w13}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{rmse }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w14}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{nse) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w15}\SpecialCharTok{*}\FunctionTok{abs}\NormalTok{(shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{bias) }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ w16}\SpecialCharTok{*}\NormalTok{(}\DecValTok{1}\SpecialCharTok{{-}}\NormalTok{ shared}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{r)}

\DocumentationTok{\#\#\#\#\# Shared model parameters \#\#\#\#\#}

\DocumentationTok{\#\# Wind speed}

\CommentTok{\# Extract the computed density data from ggplot}
\NormalTok{dens\_data }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{ggplot\_build}\NormalTok{(}
  \FunctionTok{ggplot}\NormalTok{(shared, }\FunctionTok{aes}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{x =}\NormalTok{ wind\_speed)) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
    \FunctionTok{geom\_density}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{aes}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{weight =} \DecValTok{1} \SpecialCharTok{/}\NormalTok{ score), }\AttributeTok{fill =} \StringTok{"blue"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{alpha =} \FloatTok{0.4}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{)}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{data[[}\DecValTok{1}\NormalTok{]]}

\CommentTok{\# Find wind speed where density is maximized}
\NormalTok{optimal\_wind\_speed }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}}\NormalTok{ dens\_data}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{x[}\FunctionTok{which.max}\NormalTok{(dens\_data}\SpecialCharTok{$}\NormalTok{y)]}




\NormalTok{a\_ws }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{ggplot}\NormalTok{(shared, }\FunctionTok{aes}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{x =}\NormalTok{ wind\_speed, }\AttributeTok{y =}\NormalTok{ score)) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
  \FunctionTok{geom\_point}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{alpha =} \FloatTok{0.5}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
  \FunctionTok{geom\_smooth}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{method =} \StringTok{"loess"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{color =} \StringTok{"blue"}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
  \FunctionTok{geom\_vline}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xintercept =}\NormalTok{ optimal\_wind\_speed, }\AttributeTok{color =} \StringTok{"red"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{linetype =} \StringTok{"dashed"}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
  \FunctionTok{labs}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{title =} \StringTok{"Composite Score vs Wind Speed"}\NormalTok{,}
       \AttributeTok{x =} \StringTok{"Wind Speed"}\NormalTok{,}
       \AttributeTok{y =} \StringTok{"Composite Score"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{b\_ws }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{ggplot}\NormalTok{(shared, }\FunctionTok{aes}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{x =}\NormalTok{ wind\_speed)) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
  \FunctionTok{geom\_density}\NormalTok{(}\FunctionTok{aes}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{weight =} \DecValTok{1} \SpecialCharTok{/}\NormalTok{ score), }\AttributeTok{fill =} \StringTok{"blue"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{alpha =} \FloatTok{0.4}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
  \FunctionTok{geom\_vline}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{xintercept =}\NormalTok{ optimal\_wind\_speed, }\AttributeTok{color =} \StringTok{"red"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{linetype =} \StringTok{"dashed"}\NormalTok{) }\SpecialCharTok{+}
  \FunctionTok{labs}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{title =} \StringTok{"Density of Wind Speed for Low Composite Score"}\NormalTok{,}
       \AttributeTok{x =} \StringTok{"Wind Speed"}\NormalTok{,}
       \AttributeTok{y =} \StringTok{"Weighted Density"}\NormalTok{)}

\NormalTok{a\_ws}\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{b\_ws}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

These optimized parameters were implemented as initial parameters in a
new configuration file (\emph{LakeEnsemblR\_EERES\_calibrated.yaml}).
Note that calibration can be more extensive using different calibration
methods and reiterating the simulation and evaluation process. However
this would exceed the scope of the project and may lead to overfitting.
Nevertheless calibration can be complex problem since different equally
valid methods may lead to different calibrated values (See Appendix).
The rather simple calibration method shall suffice for the purpose of
applying the LakeEnsembleR package in practice.

\subsection{Calibrated Model Run}\label{calibrated-model-run}

Followingly, the ensemble was run with the calibrated parameters. It is
suggested to set the parameter \texttt{nlev} to 6 for the model GOTM in
the calibration to set the amount of layers that should be modelled to
0.3 m / 6 = 0.05m. This avoids the internal computation resulting in the
output of only 2 layers. However, this did not avoid the lack of output
at certain depths.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\NormalTok{config\_file }\OtherTok{=} \StringTok{"LakeEnsemblR\_EERES\_calibrated.yaml"}
\NormalTok{model }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{c}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{"FLake"}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{"GOTM"}\NormalTok{,}\StringTok{"Simstrat"}\NormalTok{)}
\FunctionTok{export\_config}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{config\_file =}\NormalTok{ config\_file, }\AttributeTok{model =}\NormalTok{ model)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
##   depths wtemp
## 1   0.30 20.49
## 2   0.25 20.56
## 3   0.20 20.63
## 4   0.15 20.68
## 5   0.10 20.69
## 6   0.05 20.67
\end{verbatim}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\FunctionTok{run\_ensemble}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{config\_file =}\NormalTok{ config\_file, }\AttributeTok{model =}\NormalTok{ model, }\AttributeTok{parallel=}\NormalTok{T, }\AttributeTok{ncores=}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{verbose =} \ConstantTok{FALSE}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\section{Analysis}\label{analysis}

For a first glimpse, the heatmap of the temperature time series for each
model and the observed temperature time series were plotted.

Some models show significant technical problems, when modelling ponds of
such shallow depth. In this iteration, the GOTM model results only
represent data up to a depth of 15cm.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\FunctionTok{ggsave}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}output/ensemble\_heatmap.png\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, p1,  }\AttributeTok{dpi =} \DecValTok{300}\NormalTok{,}\AttributeTok{width =} \DecValTok{384}\NormalTok{,}\AttributeTok{height =} \DecValTok{280}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{units =} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}mm\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}

We see that only the model FLake is able to provide results with a
visible vertical stratification of water temperature. All models seem to
show lower temperature than observed data. To further investigate this,
we looked at the water temperature time series at each depth against the
observed time series. The plotting of the temperature at sediment level
using \texttt{depth=0.3} was not possible, probably for the reason
already stated above.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Plot ensemble means}
\NormalTok{plot5 }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{plot\_ensemble}\NormalTok{(ncdf,model,}\AttributeTok{var=}\StringTok{"temp"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{depth=}\FloatTok{0.05}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{plot10 }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{plot\_ensemble}\NormalTok{(ncdf,model,}\AttributeTok{var=}\StringTok{"temp"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{depth=}\FloatTok{0.10}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{plot15 }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{plot\_ensemble}\NormalTok{(ncdf,model,}\AttributeTok{var=}\StringTok{"temp"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{depth=}\FloatTok{0.15}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{plot20 }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{plot\_ensemble}\NormalTok{(ncdf,model,}\AttributeTok{var=}\StringTok{"temp"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{depth=}\FloatTok{0.20}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{plot25 }\OtherTok{=} \FunctionTok{plot\_ensemble}\NormalTok{(ncdf,model,}\AttributeTok{var=}\StringTok{"temp"}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{depth=}\FloatTok{0.25}\NormalTok{)}

\CommentTok{\# following plotting might exceed the timeout limit of the graphics device. }
\CommentTok{\# This can be avoided by rerunning the line of code.}
\NormalTok{p2 }\OtherTok{=}\NormalTok{ plot5 }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ plot10 }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ plot15 }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ plot20 }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ plot25 }\SpecialCharTok{+}\NormalTok{ plot25 }\SpecialCharTok{+} \FunctionTok{plot\_layout}\NormalTok{(}\AttributeTok{ncol=}\DecValTok{2}\NormalTok{)}
\NormalTok{p2}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\includegraphics{ACP5_PondModel_files/figure-latex/PlotEnsembleOUptput-1.pdf}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\FunctionTok{ggsave}\NormalTok{(}\StringTok{\textquotesingle{}output/time\_series\_at\_depths.png\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{, p2,  }\AttributeTok{dpi =} \DecValTok{300}\NormalTok{,}\AttributeTok{width =} \DecValTok{280}\NormalTok{,}\AttributeTok{height =} \DecValTok{350}\NormalTok{, }\AttributeTok{units =} \StringTok{\textquotesingle{}mm\textquotesingle{}}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

The plots suggest that the impact of random discrepancies is lower than
the impact of systematic discrepancies. For all depths, the models tend
to underestimate the water temperature in varying degrees. Especially
during the winter months and in the deeper layers, the models show a
stronger underestimation of the temperature. This might result from the
lack of representation of absorbed short-wave radiation, when the bottom
depth is higher up in the photic zone. The models might not be able to
capture the stratification of the water temperature in the pond in
winter months. This potentially changes when the modelling of ice is
integrated using the parameter \texttt{ice\ =\ true}.

This can be inspected in even more detail by plotting the residuals at
each depth using the \texttt{plot\_resid} function.

\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\includegraphics{ACP5_PondModel_files/figure-latex/modelquality-2.pdf}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Plot residuals vs. day of year}
\NormalTok{plots[[}\DecValTok{3}\NormalTok{]]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\includegraphics{ACP5_PondModel_files/figure-latex/modelquality-3.pdf}

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Plot residuals vs. distance}
\NormalTok{plots[[}\DecValTok{4}\NormalTok{]]}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\includegraphics{ACP5_PondModel_files/figure-latex/modelquality-4.pdf}

FLake shows the highest variance of residuals. All models tend to
systematically deviate when higher temperatures are observed, depicted
as artifacts of downward trending lines in the ``Observed
vs.~Residuals'' plot. Positive residuals for FLake can be found at
temperatures around between 15° C and 20° C. This is similar for the
predictions of Simstrat at deeper depths. However at lower depths,
Simstrat and GOTM seem to overestimate temperatures below 10° C. These
results should be carefully interpreted, because a substantial time
interval for data with approximately these temperatures in the late
summer is missing. In the ``Year day vs.~Residuals'' plot we see, that
the deviation of FLake changes with seasons. The predictions of FLake in
later spring to early summer overshoot the observed temperature
especially at lower depths. This may be explained by the overestimation
of the meteorological impact at deeper depths. The fitness of the model
to represent lower layers of shallow ponds is questionable, due to the
impact of the outer edge of the thermally active layer of the bottom
sediments. The parameters \texttt{depth\_bs\_lk} and \texttt{T\_bs\_lk}
should be part of a sophisticated calibration (default values:
\texttt{depth\_bs\_lk} = 5 m and \texttt{T\_bs\_lk} = 4° C).

The model fit can be extracted with the function \texttt{analyse\_ncdf}
as in the following code.

\begin{Shaded}
\begin{Highlighting}[]
\CommentTok{\# Analyse the netCDF output}
\NormalTok{out }\OtherTok{\textless{}{-}} \FunctionTok{analyse\_ncdf}\NormalTok{(ncdf, }\AttributeTok{model =}\NormalTok{ model, }\AttributeTok{spin\_up =} \DecValTok{0}\NormalTok{)}
\end{Highlighting}
\end{Shaded}

\begin{verbatim}
##      model Pearson_r Variance_obs Variance_mod   SD_obs   SD_mod Covariance
## 1    FLake 0.9032928     36.04043     41.95187 6.003444 6.477108   35.12361
## 2     GOTM 0.9759995     41.81463     46.92658 6.466598 6.850483   43.23378
## 3 Simstrat 0.9704949     37.95024     44.89599 6.160471 6.700550   40.05938
##        Bias      MAE     RMSE       NSE lnlikelihood
## 1 -2.282729 3.229266 3.599434 0.6405169   -291696.85
## 2 -2.562256 2.672528 2.973014 0.7886192    -98743.36
## 3 -1.054773 1.555120 1.959592 0.8988149    -92149.10
\end{verbatim}

The results match the analysis of the previous results, suggesting that
Simstrat seems to most accurately represent the observed water
temperature. Although the Pearson Correlation coefficient \emph{r} of
GOTM is slightly higher than the \emph{r} of Simstrat, the more
comprehensive Nash--Sutcliffe model efficiency coefficient (NSE) shows a
more distinct measure of the capability to predict the water
temperature, where Simstrat is about 14\% more efficient than GOTM.
These results might change when the results of all depths can be
extracted from GOTM. The generally high \emph{r} and differing model fit
parameters support the statement, that the systematic discrepancies
exceed the random discrepancies.

This work shows that the modelling of shallow pond systems is not
readily applicable to the lake models in LakeEnsemblR. While two models
generally failed to produce results for this scenario, three models
could apply this scenario after a thorough preparation of the data and
parameters. Despite the possibility to run these models, the pacakge
inherits a lot of technical difficulties to represent the results using
the internal analysis functions. The results of this work suggest, that
when those problems are overcome, LakeEnsemblR is capable to deliver a
wide foundation for further analysis of the random and systematic
discrepancies of the predictions. Some parameters were suggested to be
evaluated in more detail due to the impact in shallow pond systems.

\subsection{Single model runs}\label{single-model-runs}
